assumptions: Local capacity is intentionally set to 2 GiB to force overflow. A real H100 node has far more DRAM; this scenario exists only to exercise the remote path.
One compute node and one shared pool keep the event stream small enough to inspect by hand.
The workload is synthetic KV-cache decode derived from Llama-3-70B geometry, not a captured trace.
The compute tokens_per_second field is omitted, matching examples/llama-70b-cxl.json. Request duration is therefore driven by modeled memory accesses, not accelerator throughput.
description: Minimal overflow scenario: one compute node has a deliberately small local tier, so even a single KV cache exceeds local capacity and must use the shared pool. This verifies the remote path, eviction, and traffic accounting. It is not a hardware recommendation and must not be used for absolute performance claims.

provenance.method: One-way latency and sustained bandwidth for a CXL.mem class link; queue depth and in-flight limits are scenario assumptions.
